extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency officials responsible for preparing and submitting documents to the Office of the Federal Register (liaison officers, certifying officers, document drafters, legal/approval staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for agencies on preparing, certifying, routing, and submitting documents for filing, public inspection, and publication in the Federal Register and for drafting materials subject to codification in the Code of Federal Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison duties (§16.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency liaison officer shall represent the agency in all matters relating to submission of documents to the Office of the Federal Register and general compliance; be responsible for distribution and use of Federal Register drafting and publication assistance information; promote agency participation in technical instruction authorized by §15.10; and be available to discuss submitted documents with FRA editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liaison officers act as the agency point of contact for OFR matters, must ensure internal distribution of FR guidance, encourage staff training, and be accessible for editorial discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifying officer duties (§16.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency certifying officer is responsible for attaching the required number of true copies of each original document submitted to the Office of the Federal Register and for making the certification required by §§18.5 and 18.6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certifying officer must ensure certified copies accompany originals and that certification wording and signature authority comply with the cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt and processing hours (§17.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of the Federal Register receives documents only during official working hours unless special arrangements are made; upon receipt each document is held for confidential processing until filed for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan deliveries during working hours; expect confidentiality until formal filing for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: File for public inspection only after processing and assignment (§17.2(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document received shall be filed for public inspection only after it has been received, processed, and assigned a publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt alone does not equal public inspection — processing and scheduling are prerequisites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular schedule cutoff and assignment (§17.2(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents received by 2:00 p.m. that meet chapter requirements are assigned to the regular schedule unless special arrangements are made or the Office determines a deferred schedule is required; documents received after 2:00 p.m. are assigned to the next working day’s regular schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 2:00 p.m. is the default daily cutoff for regular-schedule consideration; agencies should make special arrangements if different handling is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular schedule filing/publication timetable (§17.2(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified mapping of received date to filed-for-inspection date and published date (e.g., received Monday before 2:00 p.m. -> filed Wednesday -> published Thursday), with one additional workday when a legal federal holiday intervenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided table to plan expected public-inspection and publication dates; account for holidays adding extra workdays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate public inspection for Government in the Sunshine Act notices (§17.2(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of meeting under the Government in the Sunshine Act are placed on immediate public inspection after being received, processed, and assigned a publication date; notices received before 4:00 p.m. are scheduled to be published 2 working days later, after 4:00 p.m. published 3 working days later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sunshine Act notices bypass normal schedule for inspection but have different publication lags tied to a 4:00 p.m. cutoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency publication criteria (§17.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The emergency schedule is intended to provide the fastest possible publication of documents involving prevention, alleviation, control, or relief of an emergency situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency schedule is limited to documents that demonstrably address emergency response or relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency publication request procedure (§17.4(a)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies requesting emergency schedule publication must briefly describe the emergency and benefits of immediate publication in a letter; the Director will assign to emergency schedule when the Director concurs and it is feasible; documents assigned must be published as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be in writing (letter) and justify the emergency and public benefit; OFR feasibility/concurrence is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency publication filing for inspection timing (§17.4(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents assigned to the emergency schedule for publication will be filed for public inspection on the working day before publication unless emergency filing for public inspection is also requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If simultaneous emergency filing for inspection is desired, request it explicitly to alter the default filing-for-inspection timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency filing for public inspection criteria (§17.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may request emergency filing for public inspection for documents on regular, emergency, or deferred publication schedules; emergency filing provides the fastest public access after processing and scheduling and is a special arrangement deviating from the regular schedule; the document remains on public inspection until published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency filing is a separate special arrangement from emergency publication and must be requested and approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency filing procedure and approval (§17.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies requesting emergency filing must briefly describe the emergency and benefits to immediate public access in a letter; the Director shall approve an emergency filing request whenever the Director concurs and it is feasible; approved documents shall be filed as soon as possible after processing and scheduling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval requires Director concurrence and feasibility; requests must be in letter form with justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred schedule criteria (§17.7(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A document may be assigned to the deferred schedule if there are technical problems, unusual or lengthy tables or illustrations, or the document's size requires extraordinary processing time, or if the agency requests a deferred publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex formatting (large tables, illustrations) or agency-requested delays can justify deferred scheduling; OFR staff will notify agencies when assignment is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of deferred schedule (§17.7(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of the Federal Register staff will notify the agency if its documents must be assigned to a deferred schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may be informed by OFR when their submission requires deferred handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originals and copies required (§18.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided for Executive orders and proclamations, each agency submitting a document for filing and publication shall send an original and two duplicate originals or certified copies; if printed on both sides, one copy must be a collated, single-sided copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified copy counts and handle double-sided printing exceptions to ensure acceptable submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on combined-category documents (§18.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will not accept a document for filing and publication if it combines material that must appear under more than one category in the Federal Register (e.g., rulemaking and notice of proposed rulemaking in one document).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Split materials by category or use cross-references when related documents are published in the same FR issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and transmittal letters (§18.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document required or authorized by law for filing and publication shall be sent to the Director of the Federal Register; except for special handling, no letter of transmittal is needed; receipt dates are determined when a signed original and clear legible copies are received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only send transmittal letters when necessary for special handling; ensure originals and legible copies are delivered to establish receipt date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of document—paper quality and legibility (§18.4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A printed or processed document may be accepted if it is on bond or similar quality paper, legible, and free of adhesive or correction tape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use good-quality paper and avoid corrections/tape that compromise legibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of document—letters and press releases excluded (§18.4(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A document in the form of a letter or press release may not be accepted for filing or publication in the Rules and Regulations, Proposed Rules, or Notices categories of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft formal rule/notice documents in the required document form rather than as letters or press releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of document—digital submissions (§18.4(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Original documents submitted by telecommunication and authenticated by digital signatures consistent with applicable Federal standards and OFR technical specifications may be accepted for publication (limited to pilot projects at present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult OFR technical staff about digital submission capabilities and standards before relying on telecommunication submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copies requirements (§18.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certified copies or duplicate originals of each document must be submitted with the original; each copy/duplicate must be entirely clear and legible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure certified copies are as readable and complete as the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of certification (§18.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each copy of each document submitted, except Presidential documents or duplicate originals, must be certified with the wording 'Certified to be a true copy of the original' and signed by a certifying officer designated under §16.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact certification wording and ensure signature authority is properly designated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements (§18.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The original and each duplicate original must be signed in ink, with the name and title of the official typed or stamped beneath the signature; initialed or impressed signatures will not be accepted; digitally authenticated submissions under §18.4(c) may be accepted as original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ink signatures with printed name/title; avoid initials/impressed marks; follow OFR guidance for digital authentication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of seal optional (§18.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a seal on an original document or certified copy is optional with the issuing agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seals are permitted but not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations, tabular material, and forms (§18.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If publishing a form or illustration is necessary, include a clear legible original or a legible reproduction approximately 8 1/2 by 11 inches in the original document and each certified copy; documents with tabular material may be assigned to deferred publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide appropriately sized, legible reproductions and expect potential deferred scheduling for heavy tabular content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble requirements for proposed/final rules (§18.12(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency submitting a proposed or final rule must prepare a preamble to inform non-expert readers of the basis and purpose of the rule; the preamble must contain specified items (AGENCY, ACTION, SUMMARY, DATES, ADDRESSES, FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT, SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION) and the SUMMARY must briefly state in simple language: (i) the action being taken; (ii) circumstances creating the need; and (iii) the intended effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the required preamble format precisely and write summaries for non-expert comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary information content options (§18.12(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may include in the supplementary information: discussion of background and major issues; for final rules, significant differences from the proposed rule; a response to substantive public comments received; and any other appropriate information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the supplementary section to provide context, document changes, and respond to comments to aid public understanding and the administrative record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal or correction of filed documents (§18.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: A document filed for public inspection but not yet published may be withdrawn or corrected by the submitting agency; withdrawals or minor corrections may be made with a timely letter signed by an authorized representative; extensive corrections may require withdrawal of the document from publication; both original filed document and withdrawing/correcting letter remain on file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit timely signed letters for minor fixes; coordinate with OFR for extensive corrections involving withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of Federal Register printing errors (§18.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Register shall be corrected by notation or reprinting when the Director determines the error would confuse or mislead the reader or affect text subject to codification; the issuing agency must review published documents and notify OFR of printing errors; if the error was in the document as submitted, the issuing agency must prepare and submit a correction document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should proactively review FR publications and promptly notify OFR or submit corrections when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of expired regulations (§18.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may reinstate regulations removed from the CFR data base which have expired by their own terms only by republishing the regulations in full text in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reinstate an expired regulation, republish the full text in the FR—partial references are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates and time period statements (§18.17(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents that include an effective date or time period should either set a date certain or specify a period measured by a number of days after publication; OFR staff will compute dates measured by days after publication by counting the day after publication as one and including Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays, but if the final count falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or holiday, the date certain will be the next succeeding Federal business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose date-certain language or clearly state day-count methods; understand OFR counting rules and business-day adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date dependency on Congressional or court action (§18.17(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an effective date depends on Congressional action or a dispositive Federal court decision that establishes or changes the effective date, the issuing agency shall promptly publish a document in the Federal Register announcing the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor external legal developments and publish prompt FR notices to establish effective dates when they hinge on such events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of subjects in agency regulations (§18.20(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency submitting a document published in the Rules or Proposed Rules section shall include a list of index terms for each CFR part affected and place the list as the last item in the Supplementary Information portion of the preamble; agencies must use terms from the Federal Register Thesaurus of Indexing Terms, but may add additional terms so long as Thesaurus terms are also used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare indexing terms using the official Thesaurus; include the index-term list in the Supplementary Information last item to aid indexing and retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form requirements for Executive orders and proclamations (§19.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed Executive orders and proclamations must have a suitable title; contain a citation of the authority; conform generally to the GPO Style Manual on punctuation/capitalization/spelling; geographic names must follow the Board on Geographic Names; tract descriptions conform to BLM specifications where practicable; be typewritten on approx. 8 × 13 inches paper with specified margins and double-spaced (with exceptions); presidential proclamations must conclude with a prescribed recitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow detailed formatting, style, and authority-citation rules when drafting Executive orders/proclamations; adhere to the specified closing language for Presidential proclamations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing and approval of Executive order/proclamation drafts (§19.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed Executive order or proclamation shall first be submitted, with seven copies and a letter signed by the head or authorized officer explaining nature/purpose/background/effect and relationship to laws and other orders, to the Director of OMB; if OMB approves it goes to the Attorney General for form and legality; if AG approves it goes to the Director of the Federal Register (or, in urgent cases, the AG may transmit directly to the President); the OFR Director will check conformity to §19.1 and for typographical errors before transmitting to the President; if disapproved by OMB or AG, it shall not be presented to the President unless accompanied by a statement of reasons for disapproval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the multi-step clearance process (OMB -> AG -> OFR -> President), provide explanatory letter and enough copies, and expect additional statements if disapproved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing and certification of originals and copies of signed orders (§19.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If signed by the President, the original and two copies shall be forwarded to the Director of the Federal Register for publication; the OFR shall place the notation 'Certified to be a true copy of the original' on copies, signed by the Director or an authorized person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After Presidential signature, OFR handles certification and publication; agencies should provide required copies initially to facilitate this process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proclamations for special days/events timing and assignment (§19.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibility for preparing proposed commemorative proclamations is assigned by the Director of OMB to appropriate agencies; such proposed proclamations must be submitted at least 60 days before the observance; the Director transmits approved commemorative proclamations to the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit commemorative proclamation drafts at least 60 days in advance and follow OMB assignment instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for treaties and international agreements (§19.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: These regulations do not apply to treaties, conventions, protocols, or other international agreements or proclamations thereof by the President, consistent with 44 U.S.C. 1511.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply the standard Executive order/proclamation rules to treaties or comparable international agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Presidential proclamations and Executive orders (§19.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'Presidential proclamations and Executive orders' includes attachments referred to in the respective proclamations or orders unless the President or representative directs otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include attachments as part of the proclamation/order package unless explicitly excluded by Presidential direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual liaison officers and compliance (§20.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies (legislative/judicial agencies, executive agencies without a §16.1 liaison or wishing additional liaison, quasi-official agencies, and others the Director deems appropriate) shall appoint an officer to maintain liaison with the Office on matters relating to The United States Government Manual; each liaison officer will ensure agency compliance with part 9 and part 20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate Manual liaison(s) to coordinate Manual-related submissions and ensure compliance with relevant parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of agency statements for the Government Manual (§20.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with schedules in §20.7 each agency shall submit for publication in the Manual an official draft of the information required by §9.2 and part 20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified schedule and required content when preparing Manual statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization content and chart legibility (§20.3(a)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational information may be shown in charts if they clearly delineate structure and are perfectly legible when reduced to Manual page size; charts that do not meet this requirement will not be included; listings of heads of operating units should reflect relationships where possible; narrative descriptions duplicating charts or lists will not be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use charts for organizational structure but ensure legibility at final print size; avoid redundant narrative that duplicates charts/lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of program activities for Manual (§20.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions should clearly state the public purposes the agency serves and the programs that carry out those purposes; descriptions of responsibilities common to most agencies will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on agency-specific public purposes and program descriptions; omit generic administrative responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of information in Manual statements (§20.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide pertinent sources of information useful to the public in areas like employment, consumer activities, contracts, services to small business, and other public-interest topics; plainly identify places where the public may obtain information or make submittals or requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List clear contact points and information sources that the public can use to obtain services or submit requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, style, arrangement, and space apportionment for Manual (§20.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The form, style, arrangement, and apportionment of space for agency statements in the Manual shall be determined by the Director of the Federal Register, with the U.S. Government Printing Office Style Manual as the applicable reference for style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conform Manual submissions to OFR formatting and GPO Style Manual conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline compliance for Manual (§20.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must comply with deadline dates established by the Director for transmittal of statements and verification of proofs; failure may result in publication of outdated statements or omission of material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet OFR deadlines to avoid omission or outdated content in the Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting documents subject to codification (§21.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies that prepare documents subject to codification shall draft them as amendments to the Code of Federal Regulations in accordance with this subchapter before submission and include words of issuance and amendatory language that precisely describe the relationship of new provisions to the Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write codification-ready amendatory text (with precise issuance/amendatory language) rather than narrative summaries for OFR processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of expiration of codified material (§21.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a codified regulation expires after a specified period by its own terms or by law, the issuing agency shall submit a notification document for publication in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit FR notice to indicate expiration of codified regulations when the regulation itself provides a termination by date or law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code structural divisions (§21.7-21.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles group broadly related Government functions; subtitles may distinguish materials from overall agencies and their components; chapters are assigned to agencies and cover subject matter; subchapters group related parts; parts are unified bodies of regulations applying to specific agency functions; subparts and undesignated center heads may group related sections; sections are the basic units and may be subdivided into paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft codified materials consistent with these structural conventions to fit neatly into the CFR organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard CFR numbering and paragraph designations (§21.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard organization numbering: titles numbered consecutively in Arabic; subtitles lettered in capitals; chapters numbered in Roman capitals; subchapters lettered in capitals; parts numbered in Arabic; subparts lettered in capitals; sections numbered in Arabic within each part (e.g., §21.15); paragraphs designated by (a),(1),(i),(A),(1),(i) etc. across levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the prescribed numbering and paragraph-lettering scheme to ensure consistency with CFR format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation of numbers for expansion (§21.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where related parts or sections are grouped under a heading, numbers may be reserved at the end of each group to allow for future expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan numbering to leave room for future additions by reserving sequence slots where appropriate.
